mechanics.name: Starter compound (walls, gate, weak points, firing platforms, spawn)
mechanics.tier: T0 - pre-built when the world is created
mechanics.player_facing_summary: The world starts with a walled yard on a levelled sand or red-sand field in desert/badlands. The compound is 19 x 24 blocks with walls 1 thick and 3 tall. There's a 3x3 gate in the south wall, 9 blocks in front of the pedestal, and the command post sits at the back. Wall-top firing platforms (two halves over the gate plus a post on each flank wall) are reached by ladders on the inside. Stake walls line the outer faces every 3 blocks. Each wall has up to 3 random breaches 2-3 wide. Each flank wall has a fixed 3-wide collapsed hole level with the pedestal, and the north-west back corner has a deliberately weak 2-tall cobblestone stretch. Walls are mostly reinforced near the gate and mostly plain old masonry further away. Players spawn on the step outside the command post door, facing south over the pedestal toward the gate. The border starts 50 wide, centred on the site, and does no damage.

mechanics.teaching_hook: The walls are a funnel, not a fortress. The horde gets in through the gate, the two flank holes, the random breaches and the weak NW corner. The reinforced blocks near the gate can't be dug, but plain masonry can. Mobs climb the inside ladders, so the platforms are contested ground, not a safe perch.
mechanics.multiplayer_notes: Built once per world, and everyone shares it. The footprint is stored on the pedestal marker. Any player can repair or extend the walls.
reward_candidates: AVOID: reinforced blocks. Reinforcing is deliberately unavailable here, so handing them out would bypass that design.

mechanics.name: Command post fittings: Crafting Station, House Grid power, barrels, Waystone
mechanics.player_facing_summary: The command post is a reinforced Lost City cafe with one dark-oak door facing the yard. Inside the doorway are 4 empty barrels, and between the door and the generator is a Crafting Station. On the back wall a Culinary Generator has a Flux Plug on top and a Basic Flux Storage beside it. At first login these, plus the Flux Point by the starter Tesla Coil, are linked into a public Flux network called 'House Grid'. Upstairs is the Wave Horn at the yard window, which has reinforced glass. A Waystone stands outside, two blocks east of the door, facing the yard. The template's loot chest, campfire, banners, smithing table, cartography table and stonecutter are removed.

mechanics.name: Starter defences (Tesla Coil, Sentry, electrified gate fence) and their wave-5 failure
mechanics.player_facing_summary: Until wave 5 the base has scavenged defences. An IE Tesla Coil stands on the gate-wall top 5 blocks east of the gate, powered from House Grid. Its lever flips on by itself whenever a wave mob comes within 9 blocks. A SecurityCraft Sentry sits 5 blocks west of the gate, set to target only mobs. Electrified iron fence seals the 5-wide gate and both flank holes at full wall height. None of them hurt players. When wave 5 is cleared, all of it is removed: only cells still holding the original block are cleared, and the Sentry and its dropped item are deleted. Chat shows '[The scavenged defenses spark, seize up, and fall dark for good.]'.

mechanics.name: Wave Horn (calling a wave) and the night lock
mechanics.player_facing_summary: Right-click the note block upstairs at the yard window to start the next wave. Only that one block counts; other note blocks do nothing. It refuses with '[Wave Horn] Clear the current wave before summoning the next one.' while a wave is open or still spawning. After a game over it only says 'The horn has nothing left to call to.' A press plays the raid horn, cancels the countdown, sets the time to night and freezes the daylight cycle so zombies don't burn, then shows the wave title. Clearing the wave, or a game over, brings back day and the cycle.

mechanics.name: Spawn ring, arrival cues and underground ambushers
mechanics.player_facing_summary: Wave mobs appear a few ticks apart in a ring 48-64 blocks from the pedestal, always outside the walls. Early on the ring is squeezed to fit inside the small border, so mobs start much closer. A cave-ambience sound plays at each mob's spawn point 12 ticks before it appears, loud enough to hear across the compound. From wave 2, ambushers burst out of the ground 4-7 blocks outside a random wall, with a spray of dirt particles and a digging sound. Big waves don't arrive all at once: once 60 wave mobs are alive, the rest wait in a queue.

Each one sets Undead Nights' difficulty to wave minus 8 (capped at 40) and spawns one Undead Nights horde 70-75 blocks from the player nearest the pedestal, with a horde scream for everyone. Team progress vs per-player rewards (multiplayer). FTB Quests progress is per team, but rewards are claimed per player: dev.ftb.mods.ftbquests.util.QuestKey.forReward keys on the player's UUID unless Reward.isTeamReward(), and data.snbt:6 sets default_reward_team false with no quest overriding it. In a single party this has three effects. (a) Every member claims every reward, including XP levels, bags and amulets; quest XP feeds the shared pedestal upgrades, so a party upgrades about N times faster. (b) 'Per-player' tasks such as 'Wear It', 'Open It' and 'Thin the Horde' complete for the whole party on the first trigger, so the book can't check that each friend learned something. (c) Item hand-ins are paid once per party: 8 gold for 'Not Just Jewelry' gives N amulets. The user's 'nothing scales by player count' rule makes (a) and (c) decisions to raise. Rewards accept a 'team' setting, which pays once per party.

Flexible progression completes tasks early. data.snbt:24 and campaign.snbt:10 use flexible mode, and TeamData.canStartTasks returns true for FLEXIBLE regardless of dependencies. Examples: 'Spoils of War' (hold an Uncommon bag) is met by bags handed out before wave 1. 'A Stone That Remembers' (hold a Waystone) is met by the Waystone 'The Last Written Wave' rewards. 'Open It' fires when a reward bag is opened. Quest has a per-quest progression_mode key, so linear can be set where order matters.

FTB Quests 2001.4.22 capabilities, from the jar. Task types: advancement, biome, checkmark, custom, dimension, fluid, forge energy, gamestage, item, kill, location, observation, stat, structure, xp. Observation types: BLOCK, BLOCK_TAG, BLOCK_STATE, BLOCK_ENTITY, BLOCK_ENTITY_TYPE, ENTITY_TYPE, ENTITY_TYPE_TAG. KillTask only takes entity and count, so it can't tell wave mobs from structure mobs or bosses. LocationTask takes fixed coordinates, so it can't target the per-world base. Reward types: advancement, all_table, choice, command, custom, gamestage, item, loot, random, toast, xp, xp_levels; choice, random and loot need reward tables, and none exist under pack/config/ftbquests/quests. Quest keys for spoiler-safe reveals: hide_text_until_complete, hide_details_until_startable, invisible, invisible_until_tasks, hide_until_deps_visible, optional, guide_page, require_sequential_tasks, min_required_dependencies. Memory: invisible quests also hide their dependents.

Progress bars on custom tasks: the snbt max_progress is ignored (bounty_kills.js:211-225). A 'waves cleared n/10' or 'upgrades bought n/9' bar needs the same CustomTask.setMaxProgress plus TeamData.setProgress reflection.
